title: Restaurant software costs that add up every month
seoTitle: Restaurant software costs monthly: what adds up | ROAL
description: Restaurant software costs can hide in commissions, per-minute billing, and add-ons. Compare the real monthly spend before you choose.
question: What restaurant software costs monthly should I watch before I sign up?
answer: The biggest monthly restaurant software costs usually come from flat fees, delivery commissions, per-minute answering, and add-ons that keep charging even when orders are slow. To compare tools fairly, add up the base fee, usage fees, and any extra charges for locations, minutes, or orders. Then test the total against your own call volume and average order size.
summary: You’ll learn how to spot monthly tech costs and compare them against your own order volume.
intro:
Restaurant software costs monthly usually look small at first, then pile up from fees you did not plan for. The real cost is often not the headline price. It is the base fee, the order fee, the minute fee, the commission, and the extra add-ons.

For a pizza shop, deli, or family restaurant, that can mean paying for phone tools even on slow weeks. It helps to compare each tool on the same terms: what you pay every month, what you pay per order, and what you pay when the phone is busy.

sections.h2: What costs show up every month on a restaurant phone setup?
sections.body:
Most owners look at the first price they see. The better question is: what will this cost after a full month of real calls, real orders, and real rushes?

A simple monthly phone stack can include:
- A phone answering tool with a fixed monthly fee
- Human answering billed per minute or per call
- Delivery app commissions on each order
- Call forwarding charges from your carrier or phone system
- Add-ons for extra locations, extra users, or extra features

A quick check you can use:
1. Write the base fee.
2. Add usage fees tied to orders, minutes, or calls.
3. Add any per-location charge.
4. Add delivery commissions if you use them.
5. Add setup, if the vendor charges it.

If a vendor says “only $99 a month,” ask what happens when your phone rings 300 times and 40 orders come in. That is where the real restaurant software costs monthly start to show up. A good comparison uses your own numbers, not the marketing number.

If you want a simple side-by-side view, [Restaurant software costs monthly compared to order-based pricing](/blog/pay-per-order-vs-monthly-fee) is worth a look.

sections.h2: How much do delivery apps take from each order?
sections.body:
Delivery apps commonly charge restaurants roughly 15-30% commission per order. That means a big chunk of the ticket leaves before food cost, labor, and rent even enter the picture.

Here is a simple example you can swap for your own numbers:

| Example order | Commission rate | Fee | What you keep before food cost |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| $25 order | 15% | $3.75 | $21.25 |
| $25 order | 20% | $5.00 | $20.00 |
| $25 order | 30% | $7.50 | $17.50 |

Now scale that up. Say you get 80 delivery-app orders in a month at a $28 average order. At 20%, the commission is $448. At 30%, it is $672. Plug in your own order count and average ticket.

That does not mean you should stop using delivery apps. It means you should know what the convenience costs each month. Some owners use them for reach, then try to move repeat callers to direct phone ordering where possible.

A direct phone order taken from your live menu keeps the order in your house. ROAL does that by answering the restaurant’s phone, taking pickup and delivery orders from the live menu, and sending a clean ticket to the kitchen screen. It is one way to reduce dependence on high-commission channels.

sections.h2: Why do monthly AI phone plans feel cheap until the bill grows?
sections.body:
Many AI phone tools for restaurants charge a fixed monthly fee per location, often in the range of roughly $79 to $599, whether or not orders come in. That sounds simple, but the bill can feel heavy if the phone volume is uneven.

Use this swap-in example:
- Monthly plan: $199 per location
- Locations: 2
- Total base cost: $398 per month
- Orders captured: 30 in one location, 10 in the other
- Effective plan cost per completed order: $9.95 before any other fees

That is not necessarily bad. It depends on what the tool handles. But you should ask yourself a few practical questions:
- Do I pay the same when the restaurant is slow?
- Is there a separate setup fee?
- Is there a per-minute charge too?
- Does the price rise when I add another location?

sections.h2: How much does human answering cost over a full month?
sections.body:
Human answering services usually bill per minute or per call. That can work well in some shops, but the bill depends on call length and how many calls are picked up.

Here is a simple way to estimate it:
1. Find the rate.
2. Multiply by average call length.
3. Multiply by monthly call volume.
4. Add any extra charges for rush periods or after-hours.

Worked example:
- Rate: $1.20 per minute
- Average call length: 2.5 minutes
- Calls answered in a month: 180
- Monthly cost: $540

If your average call is shorter, the cost drops. If callers ask about hours, parking, menu changes, catering, or reservations, the time adds up fast. That matters in restaurants because one busy Friday can create a lot of short but repetitive calls.

A phone host can answer those routine questions from your menu and public info, then hand tricky calls to staff with a summary. ROAL does that and also speaks the caller’s language, but it does not take card numbers over the phone. Payment still happens at pickup or however you already take it.

A useful script line for staff is: “If it is a simple menu or hours question, let the host handle it. If it is catering, allergy-sensitive, or manager-related, send it to us.”

sections.h2: What hidden monthly fees should I ask about before signing?
sections.body:
The sticker price is rarely the full price. Hidden costs can turn a fair-looking tool into an expensive one.

Ask these exact questions before you sign:
- Is there a setup fee?
- Is the fee per location or per phone line?
- Are test calls billed?
- Do questions cost money even when they do not become orders?
- Is there a minimum monthly spend?
- Are call recordings, transcripts, or ticketing extra?
- Do menu edits cost more?
- Does the price change after a free trial period?

A quick owner checklist:
- Read the pricing page twice.
- Ask for the monthly total at your current volume.
- Ask what happens if calls double during a holiday rush.
- Ask whether forwarding your existing number costs extra.
- Ask how long it takes to turn the service off if you do not like it.

This is where a simple cost calculator helps. A tool like [the AI phone host cost calculator](/tools/phone-host-cost-calculator) can help you compare the monthly spend against your own call count and order count.

ROAL keeps the billing simpler than many monthly plans: no setup fee, no monthly fee, no per-minute fee, and no contract. The only charge is per completed order, so unanswered questions and test calls do not add to the bill.

sections.h2: How do I test the real monthly cost before I switch?
sections.body:
Before you switch anything, run a small monthly math check using your own restaurant numbers. That takes 10 minutes and can save a lot of guessing.

Use this fill-in-the-blank formula:
- Delivery commission cost = orders × average order value × commission rate
- Human answering cost = minutes × rate, or calls × rate
- Monthly AI plan cost = base fee + add-ons + extra locations
- Pay-per-order cost = completed orders × per-order price

Example you can swap:
- 60 phone orders a month
- $28 average order
- One monthly phone tool at $149
- One additional location at $149
- Delivery app commission at 20% on 25 orders

Now compare:
- Monthly plan tool: $298 before usage-based extras
- Delivery commissions on 25 orders: $140 if the average order is $28 and the commission is 20%
- Pay-per-order phone host: 60 × $0.90 = $54

The point is not that one option is always best. The point is to see which cost structure fits your volume. A slow cafe and a busy pizzeria should not be priced the same way.

If you want to test the setup without a complicated install, ROAL lets an owner paste a website, Google Maps link, or name and city at /try, then test-call the host in the browser with no sign-up needed.

sections.h2: What monthly phone workflow keeps costs down and keeps orders clean?
sections.body:
The best monthly setup is usually the one that reduces wasted minutes and mistaken orders. That means fewer long calls, fewer repeat questions, and fewer missed details at the counter.

A practical phone workflow for a restaurant looks like this:
1. Forward the restaurant number to the phone host when busy or unanswered.
2. Let routine calls be handled automatically.
3. Send catering, complaints, allergy-sensitive questions, and manager requests to staff.
4. Keep a live kitchen screen for new, preparing, and ready tickets.
5. Review call history and menu edits from one dashboard.

A good phone script for staff is: “If the caller wants hours, parking, or the menu, let the host answer. If they need a person, we take it with the summary.”

ROAL can fit into that workflow because each location gets its own phone line automatically, and the owner forwards the existing number to it. The restaurant keeps its own number, and forwarding can be turned off any time.

Before you decide, write down three numbers for your shop:
- Monthly call volume
- Average order value
- Current phone-related spend

Then compare the total to the pricing model you are considering. If the numbers make sense, [build a free test host](/try) and try it with your own menu before you put anything live.

Delivery app commissions, monthly phone plans, and human answering can each grow quickly.

faq.q: What are the biggest monthly restaurant software costs?
faq.a: The biggest monthly costs are usually fixed software fees, delivery app commissions, per-minute or per-call answering charges, and extra charges for multiple locations or add-ons. The real number depends on how many orders and calls you handle each month. To compare fairly, total the base fee and the usage fees together.

faq.q: How do I compare a monthly plan to pay-per-order pricing?
faq.a: Start with your monthly order count and average order value. Then compare the flat monthly fee against the number of completed orders multiplied by the per-order price. Pay-per-order pricing can be cheaper in a slow month, while a flat plan may look better only if your volume is high enough.

faq.q: Do delivery apps count as restaurant software costs monthly?
faq.a: Yes, because their commission is an ongoing monthly cost tied to orders. Even if there is no subscription fee, the commission can be a major part of your monthly spend. Use your own order count and average ticket to estimate the total.

faq.q: What should I ask before I sign up for restaurant phone software?
faq.a: Ask about setup fees, per-location pricing, per-minute charges, billing for test calls, and whether questions count as billable usage. Also ask how forwarding works with your current phone number and how to cancel or turn it off. Those details usually matter more than the headline price.
